newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka plans to cut defence spending in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka plans to cut defence spending in 1997.

text.p: Sri Lanka plans to cut spending on its war with Tamil Tiger separatist rebels next year after sharply increasing defence expenditure this year, government officials said on Wednesday.

"All the capital equipment is being bought this year -- long-range guns, jets, helicopters -- the most costly things," said one official. "None of the new machines have been destroyed, although they have been damaged in the fighting."

The government, fighting the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) who want an independent homeland, has allocated 44 billion rupees (US$773.69 million) for defence. This is up from this year's original allocation of 33.9 billion rupees which was increased to 48 billion rupees as fighting escalated, the officials said.

Defence spending in calendar 1997 will account for about 22 percent of total government spending of 198.9 billion rupees, according to the estimates of revenue and expenditure presented to parliament on Tuesday.
Revenue is estimated at 185.7 billion rupees.
Deputy Finance Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris will present his budget proposals to parliament on November 6 when he will explain plans to bridge the 13.2 billion rupee deficit.
Peiris has said that the government plans to cut defence spending next year because the bulk of the new arms and equipment required to fight the rebels were being acquired by the military this year.
The armed forces have lost several aircraft and boats in attacks by LTTE rebels in the past two years.
In July this year, the rebels overran a remote army base on the northeastern coast, killing or detaining almost its entire garrison of more than 1,000 men.
The rebels also seized huge amounts of arms and ammunition, including two long-range guns.
The past two years also have seen some of the heaviest fighting between security forces and the rebels, who want a homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.

Government forces seized the rebels' northern Jaffna peninsula stronghold in April after heavy fighting. Last month the military captured Kilinochchi in the northern mainland, the last major town under rebel control.

In next year's budget, the army gets 20.5 billion rupees, almost half of total defence spending, while the navy and air force get 6.7 billion rupees each. The balance is for police and civil departments under the defence ministry.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
